title: An outlaw's diary: the Commune

The subsequent days describe the swift imposition of Communist rule, the spread of propaganda, personal separation from loved ones, and a desperate flight from the city. Through diary entries, Tormay conveys the emotional impact of revolution—loss, anxiety, and the search for hope—while observing ordinary and aristocratic life disrupted by new authorities, confiscations, propaganda, and violence.
